arxiv-2210-03378.title: UU-Tax at SemEval-2022 Task 3: Improving the generalizability of language models for taxonomy classification through data augmentation
arxiv-2210-03378.creator: Injy Sarhan, Pablo Mosteiro, Marco Spruit
arxiv-2210-03378.description: Abstract This paper presents our strategy to address the SemEval-2022 Task 3 PreTENS: Presupposed Taxonomies Evaluating Neural Network Semantics. The goal of the task is to identify if a sentence is deemed acceptable or not, depending on the taxonomic relationship that holds between a noun pair contained in the sentence.

arxiv-2306-00397.title: Decomposition of the longest element of the Weyl group using factors corresponding to the highest roots
arxiv-2306-00397.creator: Rafael Stekolshchik
arxiv-2306-00397.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rafael Stekolshchik. Let Φ \varPhi be a root system of a finite Weyl group W W with simple roots Δ \Delta and corresponding simple reflections S S . For J ⊆ S J\subseteq S , denote by W J W_{J} the standard parabolic subgroup of W W generated by J J , and by Δ J ⊆ Δ \Delta_{J}\subseteq\Delta the subset corresponding to J J .

arxiv-2402-03100.title: Inter-city infections and the role of size heterogeneity in containment strategies
arxiv-2402-03100.creator: Viktor Bezborodov, Tyll Krueger, Cornelia Pokalyuk, Piotr Szymański, Aurélien Velleret
arxiv-2402-03100.description: Abstract Abstract This study examines the effectiveness of regional lockdown strategies in mitigating pathogen spread across regional units, termed cities hereinafter. We develop simplified models to analyze infection spread across cities within a country during an epidemic wave. Isolation of a city is initiated when infection numbers within the city surpass defined thresholds.

arxiv-2402-10153.title: Knowledge-Infused LLM-Powered Conversational Health Agent: A Case Study for Diabetes Patients
arxiv-2402-10153.creator: Mahyar Abbasian 1 , Zhongqi Yang 1 , Elahe Khatibi 1 , Pengfei Zhang 1 , Nitish Nagesh 1 , Iman Azimi 1 , Ramesh Jain 1 , and Amir M. Rahmani 1,2 1 Department of Computer Science, University of California, Irvine 2 School of Nursing, University of California, Irvine
arxiv-2402-10153.description: Abstract Effective diabetes management is crucial for maintaining health in diabetic patients. Large Language Models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for diabetes management, facilitating their efficacy. However, current LLM-based approaches are limited by their dependence on general sources and lack of integration with domain-specific knowledge, leading to inaccurate responses.

arxiv-2409-09004.title: Turbo Equalization with Coarse Quantization using the Information Bottleneck Method
arxiv-2409-09004.creator: Philipp Mohr, Jasper Brüggmann, Gerhard Bauch
arxiv-2409-09004.description: Abstract This paper proposes a turbo equalizer for intersymbol interference channels (ISI) that uses coarsely quantized messages across all receiver components. Lookup tables (LUTs) carry out compression operations designed with the information bottleneck method aiming to maximize relevant mutual information.

arxiv-2412-02243.title: Alignment Parameters: Quantifying Dense Core Alignment in Star-forming Regions
arxiv-2412-02243.creator: Wei-An Chen, Ya-Wen Tang, S. D. Clarke, Patricio Sanhueza
arxiv-2412-02243.description: Abstract Recent high-resolution observations at millimeter (mm) and sub-mm reveal a diverse spatial distribution for sub-pc scale dense cores within star-forming regions, ranging from clustered to aligned arrangements. To address the increasing volume of observational and simulation data, we introduce “alignment parameters” as a quantitative and reproducible method to automatically assess core alignment.

arxiv-2501-08468.title: Selective Attention Merging for low resource tasks: A case study of Child ASR Thanks: This work was supported in part by the NSF.
arxiv-2501-08468.creator: Natarajan Balaji Shankar, Zilai Wang, Eray Eren, Abeer Alwan
arxiv-2501-08468.description: Abstract While Speech Foundation Models (SFMs) excel in various speech tasks, their performance for low-resource tasks such as child Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is hampered by limited pretraining data. To address this, we explore different model merging techniques to leverage knowledge from models trained on larger, more diverse speech corpora.

arxiv-2504-13069.title: Early Accessibility: Automating Alt-Text Generation for UI Icons During App Development
arxiv-2504-13069.creator: Sabrina Haque, Christoph Csallner
arxiv-2504-13069.description: Abstract . Alt-text is essential for mobile app accessibility, yet UI icons often lack meaningful descriptions, limiting accessibility for screen reader users. Existing approaches either require extensive labeled datasets, struggle with partial UI contexts, or operate post-development, increasing technical debt. We first conduct a formative study to determine when and how developers prefer to generate icon alt-text.

arxiv-2505-16049.title: A Non-Zero-Sum Game Model for Optimal Cyber Defense Strategies
arxiv-2505-16049.creator: Dongyoung Park, Gaby G. Dagher
arxiv-2505-16049.description: Abstract In the contemporary digital landscape, cybersecurity has become a critical issue due to the increasing frequency and sophistication of cyber attacks. This study utilizes a non-zero-sum game theoretical framework to model the strategic interactions between cyber attackers and defenders, with the objective of identifying optimal strategies for both.

arxiv-2508-07859.title: The reflex instability: exponential growth of a large-scale m = 1 m=1 mode in astrophysical discs
arxiv-2508-07859.creator: Aurélien Crida, Clément Baruteau, Jean-François Gonzalez, Frédéric Masset, Paul Segretain, Philippine Griveaud, Héloïse Méheut, Elena Lega
arxiv-2508-07859.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aurélien Crida, Clément Baruteau, Jean-François Gonzalez, Frédéric Masset, Paul Segretain, Philippine Griveaud, Héloïse Méheut, Elena Lega. We report the finding of a linear, non-axisymmetric, global instability in gas discs around stars, which may be relevant to other astrophysical discs. It takes the form of an m = 1 m=1 mode that grows in the disc density distribution while the star-barycentre distance rises exponentially with a characteristic timescale that is orders of magnitude longer than the orbital period.

arxiv-2508-10727.title: Run-and-Tumble Escape in Pursuit-Evasion Dynamics of Intelligent Active Particles
arxiv-2508-10727.creator: Segun Goh, Dennis Haustein, Gerhard Gompper
arxiv-2508-10727.description: Abstract The pursuit-evasion game is studied for two adversarial active agents, modelled as a deterministic self-steering pursuer and a stochastic, cognitive evader. The pursuer chases the evader by reorienting its propulsion direction with limited maneuverability, while the evader escapes by executing sharp, unpredictable turns, whose timing and direction the pursuer cannot anticipate.

pmc-10552886.title: Hot on RAD51C: structure and functions of RAD51C‐XRCC3
pmc-10552886.creator: Barnabas Szakal, Dana Branzei
pmc-10552886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A new study by Longo, Roy et al. has solved the structure of the RAD51C‐XRCC3 (CX3) heterodimer with a bound ATP analog, identifying two main structural interfaces and defining separable replication fork stability roles. One function relates to the ability of RAD51C to bind and assemble CX3 on nascent DNA, with an impact on the ability of forks to restart upon replication stress.

pmc-11518746.title: Relationships between altitude and depressive symptoms among middle-aged and older adults in China: a longitudinal study from the China health and retirement longitudinal study
pmc-11518746.creator: Qing Ma, Wei Jiang, Qiuyan Zhao, Xin Xia, Ronghua Fang
pmc-11518746.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have consistently documented positive associations between depressive symptoms and altitude; however, a longitudinal study of these relationships among middle-aged and older adult community populations in China has not been previously reported.MethodsWe screened 17,705 subjects who met the inclusion criteria from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study database 2011.

pmc-11712809.title: Air pollution diesel particles decrease synaptosomal post‐synaptic but not pre‐synaptic proteins in mouse cortex
pmc-11712809.creator: Jose A Godoy‐Lugo, Max A Thorwald, Constantinos Sioutas, William J Mack, Caleb E Finch
pmc-11712809.description: BackgroundChronic air pollution exposure increases accelerates cognitive aging and AD risk. Synapse loss in AD correlates with decreased cognitive ability. In rodents, inhaled air pollutants decreased glutamatergic synapses, decreasing excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs), while increasing total levels of AMPA and NMDA receptor protein.

pmc-12469342.title: Effect of Yeast Polysaccharides Replacing Sulfur Dioxide on Antioxidant Property and Quality Characteristics of Cabernet Sauvignon Wines
pmc-12469342.creator: Rui Liao, Xiongjun Xiao, Huiling Huang, Kangjie Yu, Jianxia Tan, Yue Wang, Cong Li, Siyu Li, Yi Ma, Arun K Bhunia
pmc-12469342.description: This study investigated the potential of yeast polysaccharides (YPs) as an SO2 substitute by adding varying concentrations (0–250 mg/L) prior to wine fermentation. The antioxidant activity and color stability were evaluated using UV–visible spectrophotometry, high-performance liquid chromatography, and colorimetric methods.

pmc-12536730.title: Genomic profiles of Pyricularia oryzae in Sub-Saharan Africa: exploring population differences and their evolutionary implications in the region
pmc-12536730.creator: Geoffrey Onaga, Worrawit Suktrakul, Margaret Wanjiku, Ian Lorenzo Quibod, Jean-Baka Domelevo Entfellner, Joseph Bigirimana, Georges Habarugira, Rosemary Murori, Godfrey Asea, Hamidatou Euridice Tella, Gbenakpon Aubin G. Y. Amagnide, Negussie Zenna, Chatchawan Jantasuriyarat, Abdelbagi M. Ismail, Ric
pmc-12536730.description: BackgroundRice blast, caused by Pyricularia oryzae (teleomorph: Magnaporthe oryzae), is one of the most economically damaging diseases affecting rice worldwide. While the evolutionary origins and genetic structures of Asian and European P. oryzae populations are relatively well characterized, African isolates remain underexplored. This knowledge gap impedes the development of informed management strategies for rice blast in the region.

pmc-12650025.title: MSRLNet: A Multi-Source Fusion and Feedback Network for EEG Feature Recognition in ADHD
pmc-12650025.creator: Qiulei Han, Ze Song, Hongbiao Ye, Yan Sun, Jian Zhao, Lijuan Shi, Zhejun Kuang
pmc-12650025.description: Background: Electroencephalography (EEG) has been widely used in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) recognition, but existing methods still suffer from limitations in dynamic modeling, small-sample adaptability, and training stability. This study proposes a Multi-Source Fusion and Feedback Network (MSRLNet) to enhance EEG-based ADHD recognition.

pmc-12821481.title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccine Effectiveness in the Borriana COVID-19 Cohort: A Prospective Population-Based Cohort Study
pmc-12821481.creator: Salvador Domènech-Montoliu, Óscar Pérez-Olaso, Diego Sala-Trull, Alba Del Rio-Gonzalez, Laura López-Diago, Isabel Aleixandre-Gorriz, Maria Rosario Pac-Sa, Manuel Sánchez-Urbano, Paloma Satorres-Martinez, Cristina Notari-Rodriguez, Juan Casanova-Suárez, Raquel Ruiz-Puig, Gema Badenes-Marques, Laura A
pmc-12821481.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objective: Evaluating vaccine effectiveness (VE) is essential to implementing prevention strategies, and our objective was to estimate the VE of SARS-CoV-2 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection. Materials and Methods: We carried out a population-based, prospective cohort study on the Borriana COVID-19 cohort (Valencia Community, Spain) during the 2021–2023 period, considering all SARS-CoV-2 cases that occurred after the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine campaign started in January 2021 (first approach), as well as only symptomatic cases (second approach).

pmc-13166693.title: Capacity debt in palliative care: A case report illustrating longitudinal exhaustion following early engagement
pmc-13166693.creator: Richa Randhawa
pmc-13166693.description: ObjectivesEarly engagement in palliative and supportive care is widely promoted as a marker of insight, acceptance, and readiness for shared decision-making. Clinicians, however, frequently observe a paradoxical longitudinal pattern in which patients who initially demonstrate high emotional, cognitive, and decisional engagement later become withdrawn or fatigued despite preserved insight.

pmc-13374317.title: Interventions for secondary traumatic stress among mental health professionals serving trauma-affected populations: a systematic review
pmc-13374317.creator: Momina Khalid Butt, Jonas Eimontas, Neringa Grigutytė, Rizwana Amin
pmc-13374317.description: BackgroundMental health professionals (MHPs) working with trauma-affected populations face a significant risk of developing Secondary Traumatic Stress (STS), a condition mirroring post-traumatic stress symptoms due to indirect exposure to trauma. Despite the growing awareness of STS, there remains limited systematic evidence on the effectiveness of interventions specifically targeting STS among MHPs.

pmc-13404799.title: Use of α-Cyclodextrin to Produce Nanoencapsulated Curcumin to Preserve Curcumin Stability from Photooxidation While Simultaneously Enhancing Caco-2 Intestinal Uptake and Antioxidant Capacity
pmc-13404799.creator: David D. Kitts, Yigong Guo, Maidinai Sabier, Alexandra Lizares, Anubhav Pratap-Singh, Anika Singh
pmc-13404799.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Curcumin is a major bioactive component present in turmeric, attributed with a bright yellow color; however, with low solubility and susceptibility to photooxidation, many of the purported health benefits are actually limited. We developed an encapsulation delivery system to produce curcumin nanoparticles using α-cyclodextrin as a carrier and Tween 80 as a surfactant for the purpose of increasing photostability and bioavailability.

pmc-13635490.title: Type 1 segmental Darier disease unmasked by enfortumab vedotin
pmc-13635490.creator: Nina B Curkovic, Yash Kumar, Sheba Jaison Joy, Tian Zhang, Travis Vandergriff, Meghan Heberton
pmc-13635490.description: cantholytic dyskeratosis.1 Clinically, DD presents in adolescence or early adulthood with red-brown keratotic papules in a seborrheic distribution. Nail changes, such as longitudinal erythronychia, leukonychia, or ridging are also frequently present. The disease follows a fluctuating, chronic course with triggers of acute flares including excess heat/sweating, UVB, friction, stress, and certain medications (eg diltiazem, lithium, interferon alpha 2a).
